items.title: scikit-learn version 1.9 highlights: HTML representation of estimators
items.author: Probabl
items.content:
<article>In this installment of our short series on scikit-learn version 1.9, contributor Emily Chen walks through the HTML representations of estimators.

In plain English, it is now possible to get an interactive, visual view of your models in scikit-learn. In this video, Emily shows how the HTML representation makes the structure of a model clear at a glance. You can now also inspect the fitted attributes at each step. This is especially handy for nested pipelines, column transformers, and more complex configurations.

Learn more: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.utils.estimator_html_repr.html#sklearn.utils.estimator_html_repr</article>

items.title: scikit-learn version 1.9 highlights: Narwhals support
items.author: Probabl
items.content:
<article>In this installment of our short series on scikit-learn version 1.9, contributor Emily Chen explains the benefits of Narwhals support in scikit-learn.

If your data lives in pandas, Polars, or PyArrow, you've historically had to convert it before passing it to scikit-learn. This is where Narwhals comes in. Narwhals is a lightweight, extensible compatibility layer between dataframe libraries. With Narwhals support, scikit-learn computations can work directly across dataframe libraries through a common abstraction – no conversion code is required. 

In this video, Emily explains what Narwhals is, what it changes for your workflow, and the benefits.

Learn more: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.metric_at_thresholds.html</article>

items.title: scikit-learn version 1.9 highlights: Metric at thresholds
items.author: Probabl
items.content:
<article>In this installment of our series on version 1.9, scikit-learn contributor Emily Chen walks through a handy new tool: metric_at_thresholds. 

Most classifiers output a probability estimate (e.g. 70% likely), and turning that estimate into a yes/no decision means picking a decision threshold. So, how do you know what is the right threshold for your use case? Thanks to metric_at_thresholds, now it is easier than ever to explore and identify the optimal decision threshold for your specific use case.

Learn more: https://scikit-learn.org/stable/modules/generated/sklearn.metrics.metric_at_thresholds.html</article>
